PullRequest.Title: Retry failed sanity extension installs
PullRequest.Body:
Improves release sanity extension installation by:

- scoping the install action to the GitHub Pull Requests result
- retrying when that result's install action becomes available again
- retrying when a visible Marketplace error appears
- retaining page-level Uninstall detection for successful installation

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: A failed Marketplace install blocked the sanity-test critical path on a five-minute success-only timeout before every retry, repeating up to three times despite the UI already exposing failure.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Transient or visible Marketplace installation failures could leave each affected release sanity target idle for five minutes per attempt, adding up to roughly fifteen minutes before final failure.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The new Promise.race advances as soon as installation succeeds or an explicit retry/error signal appears, eliminating the unconditional five-minute failure wait before each retry while preserving serial attempts and the existing three-attempt bound.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base revision, each failed install attempt awaited only `uninstallButton.waitFor({ timeout: 5 * 60_000 })`, converted timeout to false, and the surrounding three-attempt loop could not retry until that full timeout elapsed. The changed code races installation success against the scoped install action becoming visible again and the Marketplace message becoming visible, both direct UI signals that the attempt has ended, so failed attempts can leave the critical path immediately. `UITest.run` awaits this method in desktop, server-web, dev-tunnel, and WSL sanity workflows.

Scenarios.Scenario: Release-sanity Marketplace search resolves the GitHub Pull Requests result in desktop, server-web, dev-tunnel, and WSL runs.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening Extensions, typing the query, and waiting for either the target result or a visible Marketplace message are serial prerequisites to installation. The changed filtered locator performs DOM matching on this existing path but adds no external request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query the extension Marketplace for the typed search and any user-triggered Refresh.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initial query plus at most five serial refresh cycles on the existing error path; the changed locator does not alter request count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same typed query, result/error race, refresh loop, and network cardinality existed before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The result or Marketplace error must appear before installation proceeds.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Playwright evaluates the filtered result-row and title locators in the browser page.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: A bounded wait for one named result; no per-result external calls are introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Playwright waited directly for the matching title across all extension rows.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: DOM resolution gates the install step, but the filter replaces a broader title locator rather than adding a new network or filesystem boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The extension result list size controls local selector matching, but the filter selects one named row and does not fan out Marketplace requests with row count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One query workflow per isolated sanity target. Refresh attempts remain serial, with a five-second delay and an unchanged maximum of five.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Each target uses isolated user-data/extension directories, so Marketplace and installation state should be treated as cold per target; the diff neither adds a cache nor changes query cache keys or invalidation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed lines only refine locator scope; repository call paths show Marketplace querying remains owned by the existing Extensions view.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact result-list size and browser selector cost vary, but both are small compared with the unchanged Marketplace request and no scaling boundary was added.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added DOM filter is bounded and does not increase external boundary cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: A normal GitHub Pull Requests extension installation succeeds.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The scoped Install click starts gallery installation; waiting for the action to hide, then for Uninstall to appear, remains on the sanity-test critical path. Browser/application teardown follows immediately after UITest.run.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Playwright clicks the scoped install action and polls DOM state for hidden Install, visible Uninstall, a retryable Install action, or an error message.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One click, one initial hidden-state wait, and three concurrent bounded result waits on the successful attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The test clicked the first enabled Install action and issued a single five-minute Uninstall wait.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The hidden-state wait and winning success wait gate completion; losing waits are off the critical path after success and page teardown cancels their page work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Download/install the selected gallery extension through extensionManagementService.installFromGallery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One successful gallery install request in the normal case, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The prior Install click invoked the same gallery install path once.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Download and installation must complete before Uninstall appears.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The extension management service persists and extracts the downloaded extension into the target's isolated extensions directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One extension installation in the successful scenario.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same extension installation and persistence occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Filesystem completion contributes to when the installed-state UI appears.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost is constant per sanity target: one named extension and one successful attempt, independent of result-list size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One gallery installation is active. Three Playwright waits race after the Install action hides; losing waits are bounded by five minutes but normally terminate when the page/application is closed immediately after success.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Sanity targets use isolated extension directories, so no already-installed cache avoids the install. Any gallery/download cache remains service-owned and is not changed or bypassed by these locator/wait changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the action class calls the existing extension workbench install path, and the test loop is serial and bounded.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Playwright's internal polling cadence is implementation-dependent, but the added wait count is fixed and page teardown follows success, so retained polling is not a realistic material regression.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Success retains one expensive install boundary; added DOM waits are fixed-cardinality and short-lived.

Scenarios.Scenario: A transient install failure or visible Marketplace error triggers another install attempt.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After the first action hides, the test now proceeds when Uninstall appears, the scoped Install action becomes visible again, or the Marketplace error container appears. A failed signal is followed by screenshot capture and a five-second delay before the next serial attempt.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Retry extension gallery installation after the UI exposes that the prior attempt ended.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most three serial install attempts, the same maximum as before; the diff shortens the interval after an explicit failure signal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The existing three-attempt loop could issue the same maximum number of gallery installs, but only after each five-minute Uninstall timeout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Each initiated retry remains on the critical path, but failure no longer forces a five-minute success-only timeout before retrying.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Race three browser DOM state waits to classify success, retry availability, or Marketplace error.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Three bounded waits per attempt, at most nine started over the fixed three-attempt loop; stale losers are canceled by eventual page/application closure.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only the Uninstall success state was observed, so a known failure left the workflow blocked for five minutes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The first explicit terminal signal releases the critical path early.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Capture a screenshot after a failed attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one screenshot per failed attempt, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same failure loop captured a screenshot after timeout.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Screenshot writing occurs before the five-second retry delay.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The only multiplicity is the fixed three-attempt cap per sanity target; there is no per-result or unbounded concurrent fan-out.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Gallery install attempts are serial, never more than one newly initiated by the loop at a time, and remain capped at three. Up to two losing Playwright waits per race may remain until their timeout or page closure, yielding a small fixed upper bound rather than unbounded retention.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Retries reuse the same page, extension directory, and extension-management service, so service-level partial-download caching may apply; no explicit cache/coalescing behavior is changed. Failure signals are not negatively cached.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the loop bounds and awaits prove serial execution, and the changed race directly removes the old five-minute wait when failure is already visible.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Marketplace failure frequency and whether partial downloads are reused vary by environment. This affects total runtime/network bytes, not the established fixed cardinality or serial scheduling.
Scenarios.Verdict: No introduced performance issue. The diff preserves the maximum boundary count and substantially reduces failure-path latency; this concrete regression fix was recorded separately.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the full one-file diff. Traced search, successful install, and retry/error paths through Playwright IPC, Marketplace network access, and extension persistence. No actionable performance regression was introduced; retries remain serial and bounded, while explicit failure signals remove a prior repeated five-minute critical-path wait.
